labels: human-designed RESEARCH layout (Kannan et al., MICRO 2015), not a shipped package
model_omissions: Kannan et al.'s design is a research proposal; TAP-2.5D's die sizes and powers are its model of it.

paper_reported.quote: The original placement (a) is optimal from the routing perspective (total wirelength of 67,686mm according to our evaluation). However, our HotSpot simulations show that the system operates at 115.94oC, which is thermally infeasible.

paper_settings.temperature_metric: Three statistics, kept separate and never substituted for one another: (1) TAP's selector, run_hotspot() in sundai_tap/passive_interposer.py: the maximum of stdout.split()[3::2], i.e. of the unit temperatures HotSpot prints for the run (with -grid_map_mode center from sundai_tap/util/hotspot.config); it is not by construction limited to the chip layer, and reproducing it needs the literal selector or a reviewed emulation of it; (2) the native temperatures of the real chiplet units (Chiplet_i); (3) the active (chip) layer grid peak, our J, with -grid_map_mode max.
paper_settings.wire_metric: total routed inter-chiplet wirelength from TAP's MILP router (CPLEX)

raw.label: raw reconstruction (approximate, from published figure)
raw.role: gate zero: the paper-reconstruction comparison (astra, ScienceClaw #56858). Frozen by identity.content_sha256; use it with its exact continuous geometry and rotations.
raw.uncertainty_rule: An empirical estimate under stated assumptions, per coordinate (L-infinity): the decode error measured on TAP's own panels (max offset from its 1 mm grid) + the coordinate x the relative spread of the panel's three scale estimates + the 5e-5 mm storage step, rounded up to 1e-4 mm. It covers reading the figure only; it is not a figure-to-silicon error bound, and the figure's fidelity to the authors' simulated layout is not measurable from the figure.

round_trip.criteria: Our evaluator and router on the raw reference land within the paper's own numbers: temperature within 1 K and routed wire within 2% (room #56739, item (b)2).

prerequisites: a named warden grant for the solves

the paper's statistic: TAP's literal run_hotspot selector (max of stdout.split()[3::2], with -grid_map_mode center at 64x64) or a reviewed emulation of it. It is not assumed to be chip-layer-only; the chiplet unit temperatures and our active-layer grid peak J are separate statistics (see paper_settings.temperature_metric)
the paper's package physics: HotSpot 6.0 vertical coupling, or a reviewed fix (SLAB-049 CAL-COUPLING)
an evaluation path that validates the raw centres with the continuous rules (TapGeometry.continuous_centers_for): HotSpotOracle calls keep the 0.5 mm search lattice, which refuses them
temperature.status: PLANNED, NOT RUN: SLAB-048 has no solve grant

wire.note: Consistency evidence, not identification. Routed wire depends only on differences between pin positions, so a common translation of the whole layout leaves it unchanged: agreement checks the relative geometry, not the absolute coordinates. The routes launch no thermal solver; they run a real optimizer (HiGHS) under whatever per-job accounting applies.

snapped.rule: Round every raw centre to the nearest 1 mm grid node, then make the fewest 1 mm moves that make the layout legal on the fixture (margin with halo, halo non-overlap, 0.1 mm minimum body spacing, centre lattice). Ties at that move count go to the layout closest to the raw centres (sum of squared distances), then the lexicographically smallest centres.
